content:
I was {a}born in a Dublin street, where the {G}royal drums do beat,
and the {a}loving English feet, they tramped all {G}over {a}us,
and {C}each day and every night, when my {G}father'd come home tight,
he'd in{a}vite the neighbours {G}outside with his {a}ch{G}or{a}us.

Oh, come {a}out ye black and tans, come out and {G}fight me like a man.
Show your {a}wives how you won medals down in {G}Flan{a}ders.
Tell them {C}how the I.R.A. made you {G}run like hell away
from the {a}green and lovely {G}lanes in Kille{a}sha{G}ndr{a}a.

Oh, come tell us how you show them poor Ashlon two by two,
like the Zulus they had spears and bows and arrows.
How you bravely faced each one with your sixteen-powder-guns
and you frightened them poor natives to their marrows.

Oh, come let me hear you tell, how you shamed the brave Parnell,
when you thought him well and truly persecuted.
Where are all the sneers and jeers, that you bravely let us hear,
when our heroes of sixteen were executed.

Oh, the day is coming fast and the time is here at least
when each human will be cast aside before us.
And if there will be a need, sure my kids will sing good speed,
with a verse or two of Steven Bear's chorus.
title: The Black and Tans
